transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess it’s mostly my eating that’s been… off lately. It’s probably not a big thing, but some days I realize I’ve forgotten lunch altogether, and then other days I’m standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets even though they don’t really taste right. I just thought maybe I should come in and ask about it, if that’s okay.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

I’m not completely sure about the number, doctor… I haven’t been keeping close track. It’s more that my appetite has been strange. Some days I forget lunch entirely, and other days I’ll just be standing there eating crackers or sweets, even though they don’t really taste good. I don’t know if that’s the kind of change you mean.
Do you find that you're less interested in food than you used to be?

Maybe a little, yes. I don’t mean I’ve stopped eating or anything like that… it’s just gotten kind of turned around. Some days I forget lunch completely, and then other days I’ll stand at the counter eating crackers or sweets, even though nothing tastes quite right. I’m not sure if that counts as being less interested in food.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

I don’t know that I’ve lost a significant amount, no… at least I haven’t noticed it that way. It’s more the eating itself that’s gotten turned around. Some days I forget lunch completely, and other days I’m just standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets, even though nothing tastes right. Is that helpful to tell you?
Do you ever feel guilty after eating?
Not really, no… I don’t think so. I might feel a little silly if I’ve been picking at sweets instead of making a proper meal, but I wouldn’t call it guilt exactly. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?

Not like a real binge, I don’t think. I mean… sometimes I’ll stand at the counter and keep eating crackers or sweets, and then realize I’ve had more than I meant to. But it’s not exactly a big meal or anything. It’s more that my eating’s gotten sort of mixed up—some days I forget lunch, and other days I pick at things even though they don’t really taste right. Is that what you mean?
Do you usually eat those crackers or sweets when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or upset?

I’m not sure it’s always stress, exactly. Sometimes I just sort of realize I’ve skipped lunch, and other times I’m standing there eating crackers or something sweet even though it doesn’t taste very good. I suppose being upset might make it easier to do that, but mostly it just feels like my eating is all turned around. Is that okay to say?
Do you think your mood has anything to do with when you eat those crackers or sweets?

I think it might, yes… at least a little. What really made me come in is that my eating’s gotten all turned around. Some days I forget lunch completely, and then other days I’m just standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets, even though nothing tastes right. I don’t know if that’s exactly mood, but it doesn’t feel like my normal self. Is that the kind of connection you mean?
Do you think eating those crackers or sweets helps you feel better when you're upset?

Maybe a little, but not in a real way. It’s not like I eat them and suddenly feel better. It’s more that my eating has just gotten all turned around… some days I forget lunch completely, and other days I’ll be at the counter eating crackers or sweets even though they don’t taste right. I don’t know if that counts as trying to feel better, but it doesn’t feel like my usual pattern.
Do you eat those crackers or sweets in an attempt to improve your mood?

I don’t think I’m doing it on purpose to improve my mood, exactly. It’s more… what made me come in is that my eating has gotten all turned around. Some days I forget lunch completely, and other days I’m just standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets even though nothing tastes right. I don’t know if that answers it the right way.
Do you think eating when you're not really hungry is a way for you to deal with feeling upset or stressed?

I suppose it could be, though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. I don’t always feel hungry when I’m doing it. Some days I just forget lunch altogether, and then other days I’m standing there eating crackers or sweets at the counter, even though they don’t really taste right. I’m not sure if that’s me dealing with being upset or stressed, but my eating is definitely not like it used to be.
Do you think eating is a way for you to cope with your emotions?

Maybe… I’m not sure I’d call it coping exactly. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m doing something dramatic. It’s just that what made me come in is my eating feels all turned around lately. Some days I forget lunch completely, and other days I’ll find myself standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets, even though nothing tastes right. I guess it could be tied to my emotions, but I’m not really sure.
Do you think your eating habits have changed as a way to manage or regulate your emotions?

I guess it might be, but I don’t really know that I’m doing it to manage my feelings on purpose. What made me come in is just that my eating feels all turned around. Some days I forget lunch completely, and then other days I’m standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets even though nothing tastes right. I’m sorry, I don’t know if that’s the sort of answer you mean.
Do you think you eat as a way to make yourself feel better when you're upset?

I don’t know if I’d say it makes me feel better, exactly. Maybe a little, sometimes, but it doesn’t really feel that clear. What made me come in is more that my eating has gotten all turned around—some days I forget lunch completely, and other days I’m just standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets, even though nothing tastes right. I hope that makes sense.
Do you usually feel upset or stressed before standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets?

Sometimes, maybe… I don’t always notice it before it happens. I just know my eating has been kind of all over the place. Some days I’ll miss lunch without meaning to, and other days I end up at the counter eating crackers or sweets, even though it doesn’t really taste good. I’m not sure if that means I’m stressed first, but it doesn’t feel normal for me.
Do you think your eating habits are directly related to trying to regulate or deal with your emotions?

I’m not sure I can say it’s directly to regulate my emotions. I don’t want to overstate it. What I do know is my eating has just gotten turned around lately—some days I forget lunch completely, and other days I’m at the counter eating crackers or sweets, even though nothing really tastes right. I don’t know if that answers it the right way.
Do you believe your eating habits are a result of trying to manage your emotions?

I guess… maybe a little, but I don’t really know if I’d call it managing my emotions. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. It’s more that my eating has gotten sort of turned around—like I’ll forget lunch completely some days, and then other days I’m just standing there eating crackers or sweets, even though nothing tastes right. Does that make sense?
Do you think your eating habits are related to how you're feeling emotionally?

Maybe… I think it might be, at least partly. I don’t want to make too much of it, but what made me come in is that my eating has gotten all turned around. Some days I just forget lunch completely, and then other days I’m standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets, even though nothing tastes right. So… I suppose it probably does have something to do with how I’m feeling, but I’m not sure how to explain it exactly.
Do you think your eating habits are related to trying to feel better emotionally?

Maybe some, yes… I don’t want to make it sound like I’m doing it on purpose to feel better, exactly. It’s just that what made me come in is my eating has gotten all turned around. Some days I forget lunch completely, and other days I’m standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets, even though nothing really tastes right. So maybe it is tied to how I’m feeling… I’m not sure if I’m explaining that right.
Do you think eating is something you do to try and feel better when you're emotionally upset?

I don’t know if I’d say I’m eating to feel better exactly… I don’t want to put it the wrong way. It’s more that my eating has just gotten all turned around. Some days I forget lunch altogether, and then other days I’ll be standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets, even though nothing really tastes right. So maybe it is connected to being upset, but I’m not sure I’m doing it on purpose, if that makes sense.
